description: How each Marketing Engineer run works around the agent: its task definition, weekly schedule with its owed-run check and attempt limit, the agent's time limit, how its work is counted for the run report, the 14-day window, whether the Waitlist is live, the size of a Beta Cohort invitation batch, the outreach messages it prepares, the outputs and sources its run report accounts for, the records step that saves workspace/ and ledger/ to main, and the prices behind its approximate cost. The launcher reads this file; the agent cannot write it (G8). The exchange with Mandu: docs/mandu-exchange.md. Operating the production clone: docs/operations.md. Where a Product's raw footage is: config/products.json.

schedule.why: The Founder's Mandu sitting is Sunday evening, and each week's run falls due at 16:00 that day in the Mac's local time zone. Nothing holds the Mac awake for a run, as the Founder decided on 2026-10-11, so the run happens when the Mac is awake, Sunday night or Monday morning alike: at 16:00 if the Mac is fully awake then, and otherwise once it next is. The LaunchAgent starts the launcher at the weekly time and again every check_every_minutes minutes that the Mac is running, and every such start is a check of the launcher's own records (ledger/run-reports/attempts/): it begins a run only while this week's run is still owed and the Mac is fully awake, and ends at once otherwise. Fully awake leaves out the dark wakes a sleeping Mac makes by itself, which on the Founder's Mac came every few minutes to an hour on 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11 and lasted 45 seconds at the median: launchd starts jobs in them, and a run takes minutes, far longer than a dark wake usually lasts, so one started in a dark wake would as a rule be frozen again before it could finish. 2 minutes puts the start of an owed run within about two minutes of the Founder waking the Mac. A run that the Mac's sleep cut short does not count as the week's run, so a fresh, whole run follows by itself, up to attempts_per_week attempts at one week's run; after the last, a notice asks the Founder to start one on demand. 3 attempts allow for the Mac going to sleep in the middle of a run twice in one week, and bound what one week's run can cost at three runs. Only sleep earns another attempt: a run that timed out with the Mac awake, or failed for another reason, waits for the Founder. Both numbers are the Founder's call, changed here through a reviewed change; after a change to check_every_minutes, or to the day or time, the LaunchAgent is rendered and installed again (docs/operations.md). check_every_minutes is a whole number from 1 to 60 and attempts_per_week from 1 to 7. late_after_minutes is how long after its time a run may start before its report says it started late.

agent.why: Every run must end with its report (US-ME17), so the launcher stops an agent still running this many seconds after it started, with every process the Mac's process table shows it started, and finishes the run as timed out. The seconds are wall-clock time from the agent's start, the Mac's sleep included: nothing keeps the Mac awake for a run and a sleeping Mac runs nothing, so the stop of an agent the Mac slept past the limit starts within about a second of the Mac waking, and the run report says about how long the Mac slept. Awake time is counted too, and the agent is stopped at whichever count reaches the limit first, so a wall clock set back cannot extend a run; one set forward can end it early. Basis: the limit was set while the agent ran at Codex's default medium reasoning effort, when the 46 weekly runs with the real agent that ran to their end on the Founder's Mac between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-11 took 18 to 218 seconds from the run's start to the agent's end, median 49, 35 of them under 90, and 1800 seconds, 30 minutes, was about 8 times the longest. Since 2026-10-11 the agent runs at high effort (codex.reasoning_effort in config/guardrails/runtime.json) and takes longer. The ten runs measured on that change, each a package review and the first batch's seven post Drafts, took 283 to 1,122 seconds of agent time, median 646, nine of them with four or five such sessions running at once on the Mac and one, at 428 seconds, with none of its own beside it; the investigation before the change measured 271 to 897 seconds. The limit is left at 1800 seconds. It is now about 1.6 times the longest run measured and 2.8 times the median, not 8 times: every run measured ended inside it, the longest at 62 percent of it, but a session that also carries the workflows still to be built, or runs on a busy Mac, can come near it, and the run report's Agent time line shows each run's time against it. Those ten runs were made before Listening, outreach, and filming joined the session on 2026-10-12, and no run at high effort that carries them has been measured yet. A run of the weekly schedule cut at the limit on a Mac that stayed awake waits for the Founder, as a run that failed for any other reason does; one that the Mac slept through ends when the Mac next wakes, a dark wake included, does not count as the week's run, and is followed by a fresh run by itself once the Mac is fully awake, within schedule.attempts_per_week. There is no separate, shorter limit on silence: Codex's event stream reports only whole steps, with no sign of progress inside one. The longest run went 35 seconds without an event while it worked, and nothing bounds a step but the work in it, so a long step and a stalled model stream look the same from outside. Raise the limit here, through a reviewed change, if run reports show healthy runs coming near it; it must be above zero and at most 86400, a day.

work_counts.source: Measured on 2026-10-11 with Codex CLI 0.160.0 and gpt-6-luna, started with the launcher's own Codex command: of one command's 180,000 characters of output, Codex showed the model the first 20,000 and the last 20,000, with a note that 35,003 of 45,003 tokens were cut. That is the model catalog's truncation policy for this model, 10,000 tokens, at the 4 characters Codex counts to a token.
work_counts.why: The run report shows what the launcher counted of the agent's session beside the agent's own Review line (US-ME17), because that line is the agent's word and has read complete after the shallowest sessions. One count is how many of the package files the brief listed the agent read. Codex's event stream holds every command's whole output, whatever the model was shown of it, and a session that prints all the package files in one command is shown only the first and last of them. So the launcher counts a file as read only when at least half of its lines of 24 characters or more came back in the part of some command's output that Codex shows the model: the whole output up to this many characters, else its first and last halves of this many. A file with no line that long is counted only when a command that names its path was shown its whole text, since its short lines are in any output. The launcher sets no output limit of its own. This figure describes Codex, so measure it again and change it here, through a reviewed change, after a Codex upgrade or a change of model. The other counts need no setting: agent time, and the Draft claims and the queued package-change proposals, each counted only in what this session wrote or changed, told by one reading of each due Draft's and each incoming file's fingerprint before the agent starts and one once it has ended, so a Draft or a proposal an earlier run left is not counted as this session's. The counts inform the Founder and gate nothing.

window.why: Day 1 of the 14-day window follows from the Founder's sitting: first_sitting is the date (YYYY-MM-DD, on the schedule's day) of the sitting that approves the window's first batch, day 1 is the day after it, and every calendar day follows from day 1. Which sitting that is, and the window's one fixed evening posting slot (HH:MM, the Mac's local time), are the Founder's call (FR-8), set here through a reviewed change and never inferred, since nothing posts before the Waitlist is live; the kit's posting-slot rule in the calendar names no time, so the time is set here. Until first_sitting is set, every run prepares calendar days 1 to 7 as the first batch, with no slot; once it is set, each run prepares the calendar days that fall in the week after the coming sitting, and a post's slot is its date at this time once slot is set too.

waitlist.why: No public post may go out before the Waitlist is live (FR-9). live_since is the date (YYYY-MM-DD) the Waitlist went live, set here through a reviewed change once US-ME05's Validation Test has passed on reptoday.app, and never inferred from whether a source is connected or what it is named. While it is null, or a date still ahead, every post item, the run brief, and the run report say that nothing can be published until the Waitlist is live.

beta_recruiting.why: How many Waitlist entries one Beta Cohort invitation batch offers the Founder (US-ME15), the Founder's call, changed here through a reviewed change. The Founder confirmed capped batches and chose 20 on 2026-10-11. At most one batch is open at a time, and the next is offered only after the Founder has decided the last, so a week's sends and first sessions stay manageable. It cannot be larger than the cohort's maximum in config/products.json.

outreach.why: The personal-network ask carries the link of the Source tagged network_ask_source, exactly as the reviewed Waitlist Dispatch request in src/dispatches/ defines it; null prepares no ask. creators are the three the PRD names, each with the key its Draft file and its Review Queue items are named for; a run drafts a message only for one the channel plan in Mandu still names (the Product registry's outreach.channel_plan). A creator who has not replied may be offered one follow-up follow_up_wait_days after the Founder records the first message as sent in Mandu: each creator message states that period, approving it approves the period, and the Founder's record may set another.

records.why: Only the production clone syncs and saves records; every other checkout runs without touching git. Setting sync_before_run or save_after_run to false turns that step off.

cost.why: The run report states the run's approximate cost at API prices from Codex's token counts.
